post.description:
Read a stream by whatever delivers it, or publish one that has no source of its own, given the protocols the caller can play or send, in its order of preference: the exposure to read or publish (`exposureId`, at `gatewayId`) and its `connection`, as `organisations.streams.exposures.connect` gives one. Ask again before `connection.expiresAt`: the answer may name another exposure.

Reading: the candidates are the stream's exposures on gateways the caller reaches, read by a protocol it named: a gateway on no network is on the internet, reached by everyone, and one on a network is reached by a device on that network alone, so a member's browser reaches internet gateways only. An output's agent reads only from its output's input gateway, when it names one. Of those, one on the caller's own network is preferred, then conservation.tv, then any other internet gateway; exposures whose health is failing come last, and for a stream with no source, after them any its gateway says is not live. Members read, signed in. Devices call with an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by their own identity: an output's agent reads what the show its output follows places, or under `external` control any of its organisation's streams.

Publishing (`action: publish`): only a stream with no source device (`not_pushed` otherwise). The gateway is chosen as a reader's is, from those the publisher reaches (the internet, and the network it names as `networkId`) published to by a protocol it named, and the stream's exposure there is made if it has none, with one at conservation.tv that the gateway's agent republishes it to when it is elsewhere; both are kept for the next time. Members with the right to publish (`streamPublisher`, which administrators hold), signed in, or their browser's own device (`organisations.browser.ensure`) signing for them; a member's own stream (`organisations.streams.personal.ensure`) is published by that member alone (`forbidden` for anyone else). A new exposure at a MediaMTX gateway is served once its agent next asks for its configuration, within about half a minute: until then publishing there is refused, so try again.

put.summary: Get where an encoder publishes a stream
put.description: Members with the right to publish (`streamPublisher`, which administrators hold), for a stream with no source device (`not_pushed` otherwise); a member's own stream (`organisations.streams.personal.ensure`) only for that member (`forbidden` for anyone else). get.description: What the signing device runs, derived from the topology whenever it asks: a section for each runtime it is to run, and none for those it isn't. `mediamtx`, for a network's active agent on a network with a MediaMTX gateway: the gateway (and how it checks readers' tokens), the MediaMTX `paths` it serves, each delivering an exposure from a `source` that is a URL to pull while it is read (a camera's, credentials included) or another of its paths, the `publishers` it runs, each publishing an exposure by MoQ from one of its paths, with the `connect` ask for where to publish and the token to do so, and the `stats` asks (`organisations.gateways.stats.connect`) for the traffic stats of the gateways it publishes to that publish them. `obs`, for the agent an output runs on (`organisations.outputs.setDevice`): the `output`, its organisation, and its `control`, who drives OBS's scenes (`show`: the `show` runtime; `external`: something outside the studio, which reads how to reach OBS from `organisations.outputs.control.get`, the agent having reported it with `organisations.outputs.control.report`, and plays any of the organisation's exposures through it), the `encoding` the programme is sent at, the `forwards`, one for each channel the output has an enabled forward to, naming the forward and the channel whose server and stream key it reads with `organisations.channels.ingest`, and whether the channel has `stats` it reads with `organisations.channels.stats.get` and reports about `channel:<channelId>`, the `previews` it publishes the programme to, each with the `connect` ask (`organisations.outputs.previews.connect`) for where to and its token, the `recording` it makes alongside streaming, when the output has a recorder, and the `program`'s subject ID, to report about it against; it reads each exposure OBS plays with `organisations.streams.exposures.connect`. `show`, for that agent while the output follows a show under `show` control: the show's `id`, and the `url` it signs a WebSocket upgrade to as the device to follow it. A device with no section runs nothing. Any device: the request carries an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by the device's Ed25519 identity, as for `reports.submit`, over an empty body. From version 3 the agent is given its cameras as they are registered, rather than URLs made from them. `cameras`, for a network's active agent: the cameras on its network and those its streams are pulled from, each with the `settings` its driver reads, its `credentials`, and its `state`, and the `issuer` of the grants that admit commands to them: it controls an `enabled` one for whoever presents a grant this API signed as the agent, for the agent, to the presenting device (`organisations.cameras.control.connect`). A `mediamtx` path's `source` is then a `cameraId` to pull, or another path, and each of its `probes` a `cameraId` to ask. `chat`, for an output's agent while the output goes out to a Twitch channel and the organisation has chat commands: the `channels` whose chat to listen to, by login, and the `commands` to listen for, each told to this API when used (`organisations.chatCommands.trigger`). `peers`, always: every other agent and browser of the organisation, by endpoint ID, with whether each may connect directly or through the relay alone; the agent serves no one else. Each of `obs`'s `previews` also has its `signer`: the key ID of the agent that signs tokens for its gateway, the network's active agent for a MediaMTX gateway, or null for a built-in gateway or one no agent runs; a token kept for a preview is asked for again when it changes, as when another agent becomes the network's active agent. From this version each of `mediamtx`'s `publishers` names the one `path` it reads, and publishes it as one broadcast, whose catalog says what it carries; and `mediamtx` has no `stats`. `relays`, for an agent that covers some of the organisation's exposures on a gateway whose relays publish stats (each such exposure is covered by exactly one agent: the one that delivers it, otherwise the organisation's oldest active agent): the `stats` asks (`organisations.gateways.stats.connect`) for each such gateway, and the exposures it covers but does not publish (`watched`), each with the `connect` ask (`organisations.streams.exposures.connect`, `action: read`) to read its catalog back through the relay by. It reports what the relays carry of every exposure it covers, and whether they have it.

post.description:
Read a stream by whatever delivers it, or publish one that has no source of its own, given the protocols the caller can play or send, in its order of preference: the exposure to read or publish (`exposureId`, at `gatewayId`) and its `connection`, as `organisations.streams.exposures.connect` gives one. Ask again before `connection.expiresAt`: the answer may name another exposure.

Reading: the candidates are the stream's exposures on gateways the caller reaches, read by a protocol it named: a gateway on no network is on the internet, reached by everyone, and one on a network is reached by a device on that network alone, so a member's browser reaches internet gateways only. An output's agent reads only from its output's input gateway, when it names one. Of those, one on the caller's own network is preferred, then conservation.tv, then any other internet gateway; exposures whose health is failing come last, and for a stream with no source, after them any its gateway says is not live. Members read, signed in. Devices call with an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by their own identity: an output's agent reads what the show its output follows places, or under `external` control any of its organisation's streams.

Publishing (`action: publish`): only a stream with no source device (`not_pushed` otherwise). The gateway is chosen as a reader's is, from those the publisher reaches (the internet, and the network it names as `networkId`) published to by a protocol it named, and the stream's exposure there is made if it has none, with one at conservation.tv that the gateway's agent republishes it to when it is elsewhere; both are kept for the next time. Members with the right to publish (`streamPublisher`, which administrators hold), signed in, or their browser's own device (`organisations.browser.ensure`) signing for them; a member's own stream (`organisations.streams.personal.ensure`) is published by that member alone (`forbidden` for anyone else). A new exposure at a MediaMTX gateway is served once its agent next asks for its configuration, within about half a minute: until then publishing there is refused, so try again.

get.description: Whether the organisation is working, and what is wrong if not. Each subject's own status is from its state (`failing` is reporting unhealthy, or gone quiet; `idle` and `off` aren't judged, since nothing asks for it or it is switched off; `unknown` has reported nothing to judge by); failures then flow along the signal's path, from a camera through its stream's deliveries, and from an output's agent through its programme to its forwards, previews, recorders and channels, so what a failing subject feeds is `affected` (`causedBy` what) rather than a problem of its own. A subject nothing is set to report about (an output with no agent's parts, a delivery no agent delivers, a camera no agent probes, a camera that is switched off and its streams' deliveries, a forward that is switched off) is `off`, whatever was last said of it, and says why. `streams`, `shows` (the sources and deliveries of the streams each places), `outputs` and `channels` sum their parts up, each in a sentence, and `status` and `summary` the whole. `problems` are only the root causes: each subject failing or degraded itself, why (`reasons`, its state's findings in words), and what that affects.

get.description: How it is operated (`slots`, its layout; `volumeDb` and `muted`, its own mix; `takeoverStreamId`, the stream armed to take over, and `takeoverLive`, whether it has), the outputs following it, and its `lineup`: the camera streams of the organisation, and its pushed streams (going live from a phone, a PC or OBS) while someone publishes them, as the health of their deliveries says. Those in the lineup come first, in position order (the first `slots` are on screen), then those out of it, each with why (`absence`: a pushed stream waiting to be swapped in, `standby`; a camera that is `locked` or `disabled`; or nothing delivering it, `undelivered`), and each with how the show mixes its sound. A camera that is unlocked, or new, joins the lineup at the end; a pushed stream is never placed by itself, and leaves the lineup once nobody publishes it. `takeoverMix` is how the show mixes the stream armed to take over, as a lineup entry says it but for where it is (null with none armed): a stream that is not in the lineup has its level and mute here. `unreachable` says, for each output following the show that has an agent (an output with none reads nothing, and is left out), which of the streams the show needs its agent reaches no delivery of (`streamIds`, empty when it reaches them all): the cameras on screen, the stream armed to take over, and any stream one of those brings the sound of, each with at least one delivery but none at a gateway the agent reaches, from its network or the internet, and only at the gateway the output reads from when it names one (`inputGatewayId`). The output still places such a stream, so its card shows there. Protocols are not considered: which an agent asks with is its own.

post.description: Any member. `a` and `b` each name a stream in the lineup, by its ID or its position (from 1), or a pushed stream on standby by its ID, resolved against the lineup as it is when the swap is made; the two exchange places wherever they are: both on screen, or one off it, which is how a camera is brought on. Refused (`invalid_reference`) for a stream that is neither in the lineup nor on standby, or a position past both. Returns the lineup after, as `organisations.shows.get` reads it.
